title: Promises and the event loop
summary: Why some JavaScript runs later, in what order, and how async/await reads like normal code.

sections.heading: Some code runs later
body: JavaScript runs one thing at a time. `setTimeout` does not pause; it schedules a function for later and carries on. Even with 0 milliseconds, it waits until the current code has finished.

sections.heading: Promises go before timers
body: There are two waiting lines. Promise callbacks (`then`, code after `await`) go in a fast line that is emptied as soon as the current code finishes. Timers wait in a slower line after that.
So the order is: plain code first, then promise callbacks, then timers.

sections.heading: async and await
body: `await` pauses only the `async` function it is in, until the promise is done. The code that called that function keeps going straight away.

mistakes: Forgetting `await`, so you get a pending Promise instead of the value.
Thinking `await` freezes everything. It only pauses its own function.
